::: {#thm-inner-product-sign}

#### The sign of the inner product

For nonzero $\vx, \vy \in \reals^p$ with [angle](#def-angle) $\angpar \in [0, \pi]$ between them,

$$\dprod{\vx}{\vy} = \norm{\vx}_2 \norm{\vy}_2 \cos\angpar,$$

so:

- $\dprod{\vx}{\vy} > 0$ when the vectors point broadly in the same direction ($\angpar < \pi/2$).
- $\dprod{\vx}{\vy} = 0$ exactly when the vectors are orthogonal ($\angpar = \pi/2$).
- $\dprod{\vx}{\vy} < 0$ when the vectors point broadly in opposing directions ($\angpar > \pi/2$).

:::

::: proof
By the definition of the angle, $\cos\angpar = \dprod{\vx}{\vy} / (\norm{\vx}_2 \norm{\vy}_2)$,
which gives the identity.
The product $\norm{\vx}_2 \norm{\vy}_2$ is positive because both vectors are nonzero,
so $\dprod{\vx}{\vy}$ has the sign of $\cos\angpar$.
On $[0, \pi]$, the cosine is positive for $\angpar < \pi/2$, zero at $\pi/2$ and negative for $\angpar > \pi/2$.
:::
